research_caveat: IMPORTANT: no Stripe primary source could be consulted in this session AT ALL. (1) The sandbox network gateway (agent proxy) returned 403 CONNECT denials — egress-policy denials, which the proxy README instructs must not be retried or routed around — for every Stripe host attempted: stripe.com (privacy policy at /privacy), docs.stripe.com (/security), and support.stripe.com. WebFetch got HTTP 403 on https://stripe.com/privacy and https://docs.stripe.com/security, and direct curl through the proxy confirmed 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' for stripe.com:443, docs.stripe.com:443, and support.stripe.com:443 — the same policy denial recorded for slack.com, salesforce.com, usepylon.com etc. in the proxy status log. (2) The session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200, consumed by sibling vendor researchers) before any Stripe search could run, so the domain-restricted-search-snippet fallback used by earlier vendor files was unavailable. Per the researcher hard rules ('if you did not fetch a URL stating the fact for THIS vendor in THIS session, the value is Not known'), every Bucket A field below is 'Not known' with confidence 'none'. This is a statement about this session's network access, not about Stripe's documentation, which is extensive (privacy policy at stripe.com/privacy, security docs at docs.stripe.com/security, DPA at stripe.com/legal/dpa, Privacy Center at stripe.com/legal/privacy-center). A re-run from an unrestricted network (or with search budget) should be able to fill most of these fields from Stripe's own pages before falling back to the written vendor questionnaire. VERIFIER (2026-07-31): both stated causes independently reproduced this session, not taken from this caveat — WebFetch 403 on https://stripe.com/privacy and https://docs.stripe.com/security; curl 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403' on stripe.com:443, docs.stripe.com:443, support.stripe.com:443 (hosts present in the proxy status denial log); WebSearch refused at 200/200 budget; archive/mirror fallbacks (web.archive.org incl. a direct /web/2026/stripe.com/privacy probe, r.jina.ai, dataprivacyframework.gov) also gateway-denied 403. Zero sourced claims existed to verify and zero upgrades were possible. NOTHING from this file may be written to the workbook until a re-run from a network that can reach Stripe domains (or Stripe's written answers arrive).

USA and UK) at similar quality — no such alternative sub-processor chain exists for real-time conversational video AI; the competitive supply chain (GPU inference, voice models, WebRTC) is US-controlled. (b) Not inconsistent with 3.2.1=Yes for hyperscalers: an EU region changes where data sits, not who controls it — a US parent remains subject to US legal process with US-based administrative access, so USA transfer is not 'excluded' by region choice. Reliance is on SCCs/DPF + supplementary measures, not transfer avoidance.

open_questions_for_vendor: Please confirm the exact legal entity that contracts with Tavus (a US-based company) for payment processing services — full legal name, legal form, and state/country of incorporation (we believe 'Stripe, Inc.') — and provide that entity's registered office / principal place of business address.

Has Stripe, Inc. designated a representative in the EU under Article 27 GDPR (and in the UK under UK GDPR)? If yes, please provide the representative's name and full address; if Stripe instead relies on an EU establishment (e.g. an Irish Stripe entity) for EU processing, please identify that entity and its address and its role in the processing chain for Tavus data.

Have you formally appointed a Data Protection Officer? Public references point to dpo@stripe.com — please confirm this is the authoritative DPO contact entitled to respond to data-protection-related requests from customers (SAP requires a named channel), and provide the DPO's name and telephone number and/or email address.

Which certifications and audit reports does Stripe currently hold for the payment processing service (PCI DSS Level 1 — current Attestation of Compliance; SOC 1 / SOC 2 Type II — period covered and Trust Service Criteria in scope; SOC 3; ISO 27001 or other ISO certifications with scope statements)? Please provide the current reports/certificates (under NDA if required) so Tavus can place them on file.
What minimum TLS version (e.g. TLS 1.2, TLS 1.3) is enforced for data in transit to stripe.com, api.stripe.com, and Stripe Dashboard endpoints?
Which encryption algorithm and key length are used for personal data at rest (cardholder data, billing contact records, transaction records, logs)?
Are backups encrypted, and with which algorithm? Are backup encryption keys managed the same way as production keys?
Who generates and manages the encryption keys for data at rest (Stripe-managed platform keys vs. customer-specific keys)? Are keys HSM-backed, and is any customer-managed-key option offered?

Can Stripe, acting as a processor/service provider for our billing data, anonymize and/or pseudonymize personal data (e.g. card tokenization, hashed identifiers, anonymization on account closure or erasure request)? Please describe the capability and any statutory-retention limits on erasure of payment records.

Beyond encryption, which other technical safeguards protect personal data (network segmentation of the cardholder data environment, access controls and least-privilege for Stripe personnel, MFA, audit logging, penetration testing cadence, bug bounty program)?
Does Stripe offer EU data hosting / an EU Access option for customer personal data? If yes: which data categories does it cover, and is it available to a US-contracted merchant such as Tavus?
Please provide your current sub-processor list for the payment processing service (SAP requires the processing chain to Level 2, e.g. the underlying cloud infrastructure provider(s)).
